# Cost model - generated by gen/cost.py (do not edit)

**Honesty boundary.** No part has been bought or quoted. A *priced* line has a looked-up price (gen/data/prices.csv, URL and date 2026-10-04); an *estimated* line has a stated engineering basis (gen/data/cost_estimates.csv); an *unpriced* line has neither and is listed, never counted as zero. All prices are single-source web readings, not contracts. Cost per kW uses the rated power of the product (PV-01, PV-15, DAB-01). The modules PV-P75 and PV-P100-110 are the cost-first baseline (D-044/D-045: boards PV-PWR / PV-PWR-4 and PV-CTL); the modules ending in -FULL are the roadmap's earlier platform, kept for contrast.

**Catalogue price** = the break at the highest quantity <= 1000 pieces from the best source (LCSC first, then the maker's own site, then distributors, brokers and aggregators; cheapest within a class; a one-piece price loses to any source that has a volume break). Currencies at the ECB rates of 2026-10-02 (1 EUR = 1.1225 USD = 7.5259 CNY, so 1 USD = 6.705 CNY). Chip passives use reel-price class rules; custom parts use engineering estimates (copper and aluminium at LME cash of 2026-10-02: 14,355 and 3,109.5 USD/t). Prices marked 'single-piece price' are catalogue prices for one piece. A price row can belong to an equivalent part of another maker with the same type designation (its note in prices.csv says so). Confidence: high = LCSC or maker price read from its page; medium = distributor/broker price or an estimate pinned to a close equivalent; low = engineering estimate.

**Price at a 5000-unit build** (SRC-6; the annual quantity of a line is 5000 x its quantity per module). REAL = a published price of the part at a break of at least 1000 pieces and at most the annual quantity (LCSC highest break, TI.com 1ku list price, a distributor's volume tier, or the highest break of the LCSC listing that a chip-passive class is built on). ASSUMED = the catalogue price times a factor of gen/data/volume_factors.csv, chosen by part class, with its basis written out there. A REAL price is never above the catalogue price, and the highest published break can still be above what a 5,000-unit buyer would be quoted: no quote exists.

## Against the owner's benchmark (SRC-5, AC-03)

**Benchmark.** Megarevo MPHV 1500 V string PCS, 228 kW, 630 V AC, DC 914-1500 V: selling price 1,500 USD = 6.58 USD/kW (the owner's figure of 2026-10-04; source row in gen/data/market_prices.csv: https://www.megarevo.com/upload/download/1500V-String%20Power%20Conversion%20System%20V1.1.pdf). The benchmark is a *selling price* of a complete AC/DC unit; to compare it with a BOM the following assumptions are used (constants of gen/cost.py):

- BOM share of a selling price = (1 - 0.25 gross margin) x 0.80 BOM share of the cost of goods = **0.60**, so the benchmark's BOM is 1,500 x 0.60 = 900 USD = **3.95 USD/kW**.
- Current adjustment: a DC/DC module carries more amperes per kW than the benchmark (1.16 A/kW on its DC side). 70 % of a BOM scales with current (semiconductors, inductors, contactors, fuses, busbars, film banks), 30 % with power: equivalent BOM = benchmark BOM per kW x (0.30 + 0.70 x module A/kW / 1.16) x kW (ARCHITECTURE-PCS.md section 12).
- Range: the last column of the first table gives the benchmark-equivalent BOM at a gross margin of 15 % / 25 % / 30 %.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PV-P75 | 75 | 135 | 1.80 | 1.55 | 1.39 | 410 | 976 | 2.4x | 817 | 2.0x | 465 / 410 / 383 |
| PV-P100-110 | 100 | 180 | 1.80 | 1.55 | 1.39 | 547 | 1167 | 2.1x | 977 | 1.8x | 620 / 547 / 511 |

## Reconciliation of PV-P75 with the architect's list

This BOM at catalogue prices: **975.97 USD**. The architect's costed list `gen/data/costfirst_bom.csv` (PV-P75): **965.72 USD** (its rows add up to 965.72). Difference (BOM minus list) **+10.25 USD**. Rows are paired by part name (a few renamed parts through the ALIAS table of gen/cost.py). The list bundles many small parts into 'class' rows that have no single BOM line (shown as 'list only'); BOM lines the list does not name are 'BOM only'.

| step | catalogue USD | at 5000 units USD |
|---|---|---|
| architect's list, total | 965.72 | 731.25 |
| change on paired lines (this BOM 832.04 against the list 892.79) | -60.75 | +12.30 |
| plus BOM-only lines (257 lines: parts on the drawn boards that the list does not name) | +143.93 | +135.80 |
| minus list-only rows (17 rows: bundled 'class' rows and parts not drawn) | -72.93 | -62.26 |
| **this BOM, total** | **975.97** | **817.10** |

At 5000 units the two totals differ by +85.85 USD (this BOM 817.10, the list 731.25). 5k / catalogue is 0.84 here and 0.76 in the list. The list sets a 5k price per row (median ratio 0.85, lowest 0.52; its largest single reduction is L_CELL 224uH (CUSTOM): 80.00 to 55.00 USD per piece, 75 USD in total); this BOM uses published breaks of 1,000 pieces or more where they exist (mostly at the catalogue price already) and the class factors of gen/data/volume_factors.csv elsewhere.

**Which is right.** For the drawn boards, the BOM column: it prices every part that is on the schematics (the list prices some small parts as bundles), and it follows the later source where one exists. The three largest paired differences are L_CELL 224uH (CUSTOM) -118.50 USD; SG2M040170HJ +24.02 USD; 7461057 +13.80 USD. Where the basis of a BOM line reads 'architect's list', the BOM carries the list's estimate over unchanged: the two agree, and the number is only as good as that estimate (an RFQ that has not been answered).
